name: baize-dogfood-v1
description: Seed dataset (issue #17): 60 questions across the PRD §14 categories, instantiated against baize's own repository as the first fleet. Expected answers are drafts pending human review (expected.reviewed=false); cross-repo/event categories are templates until a real multi-repo estate is indexed.

questions.question: Where is the ACP WebSocket-to-stdio bridge implemented?

expected.answer: src/acp-bridge.js — createAcpBridge frames WebSocket messages to stdio JSON-RPC lines and back.

questions.question: Which function injects the CBM MCP server into session requests?

expected.answer: injectMcpServers in src/acp-bridge.js rewrites session/new|load|resume params before forwarding.

questions.question: Where does the fleet regenerate the agent's AGENTS.md?

expected.answer: prepareAgentWorkspace in src/agent-workspace.js, wired per connection from src/app.js.

questions.question: Where is the bare-mirror sync engine (clone/fetch) implemented?

expected.answer: src/sync.js — syncMirror clones/fetches bare mirrors and materializes linked worktrees.

questions.question: Where does BaiZe resolve its home directory (~/.baize)?

expected.answer: src/paths.js — BAIZE_HOME env override, defaulting to ~/.baize.

questions.question: Which module owns the code-index registry state machine (kickIndex, retries)?

expected.answer: src/repos.js — the registry with indexing states, backoff retries, and CBM wiring.

questions.question: Where is the DNS-rebinding guard that checks Host/Origin on WebSocket upgrade?

expected.answer: The upgrade handler in src/acp-bridge.js destroys non-local Host/Origin upgrades.

questions.question: Where is the first-run setup wizard UI implemented?

expected.answer: ui/src/components/SetupWizard.tsx with the phase hook useBaizeSetup.

questions.question: Who calls syncMirror and what happens on its result?

expected.answer: The sync queue in src/sync.js calls it per repo; success with a revision calls onRevision which kicks indexing via the registry.

questions.question: What calls prepareAgentWorkspace and when?

expected.answer: createAcpBridge invokes the prepareWorkspace callback before spawning the agent child on every WebSocket connection.

questions.question: Which code paths call binaryPathOrNull?

expected.answer: src/app.js's agentMcpServers closure calls it per connection; null degrades to no MCP injection with a logged remedy.

questions.question: Who consumes the onRevision hook?

expected.answer: src/app.js wires onRevision to registry.ensureFleetRepo, which registers the fleet repo and kicks indexing.

questions.question: What calls kickIndex and with which revisions?

expected.answer: ensureFleetRepo on sync revisions, and the describe() rebuild path when a stale token is found in CBM.

questions.question: Which functions does the HTTP API's /api/sync handler call?

expected.answer: handleApi in src/server.js calls sync.states() for GET and syncAll()/syncNow() for POST.

questions.question: Who calls loadDataset/extractCitations in the benchmark harness?

expected.answer: run-cli.js loads datasets; run.js's collectTurn extracts citations from answers; report.js recomputes them.

questions.question: Which service calls the baize management API from another repository?

expected.answer: Pending a real multi-repo estate — baize currently has no external HTTP callers in the fleet.

questions.notes: Instantiate against a fleet with a real consumer service once available.

questions.question: Trace an HTTP call that crosses repository boundaries in the fleet.

expected.answer: Pending a real multi-repo estate.

questions.question: Which repositories produce/consume Kafka topics in the fleet?

expected.answer: Pending a real estate with Kafka — baize itself has no message bus.

questions.question: Trace an event from its producer repo to every consumer repo.

expected.answer: Pending a real estate with message queues.

questions.question: What are the main modules of the baize server and their responsibilities?

expected.answer: src/ has ~13 flat modules: cli/app entry, server (HTTP+/fleet page), acp-bridge (agent), sync/repos (fleet), gitlab (API), cbm (index), config/paths, agent-workspace, benchmark.

questions.question: How does a chat message travel from the browser to the agent and back?

expected.answer: UI WebSocket to /acp; acp-bridge frames to omp stdio JSON-RPC; updates flow back as session/update notifications.

questions.question: What is the CBM daemon model and why does baize share one cache dir?

expected.answer: CBM runs a per-account daemon; baize's supervisor and the agent's injected server both set CBM_CACHE_DIR to the same index dir so they share the daemon and index.

questions.question: Where does the UI's session state live and how is it projected?

expected.answer: The store keeps session documents; ui/src/projector/messageStream.ts folds them into flat items (ADR 0006 identity caches).

questions.question: How is the repository laid out for publishing?

expected.answer: Single npm package: src/ server, ui/ vendored Panda SPA built to ui/dist, bin entry baize -> src/cli.js.

questions.question: What prevents the agent from reading repositories outside the fleet?

expected.answer: Only fleet worktrees are indexed and listed in AGENTS.md; the agent has no other repo access by construction.

questions.question: How does the wizard decide to show, and what can override it?

expected.answer: useBaizeSetup derives phase from /api/gitlab/settings (baseUrl+token+selection); a dismiss (skip) hides it until reload; the settings route renders ahead of it.

questions.question: What are the two UI-server channels and what rides each?

expected.answer: ACP over WebSocket (/acp) for chat; the BaiZe management API (/api/*) for fleet, sync, and settings.

questions.question: What are baize's runtime dependencies?

expected.answer: package.json lists only codebase-memory-mcp (pinned 0.10.8) and ws; Node stdio does the rest.

questions.question: Which UI dependencies does the chat stream renderer use?

expected.answer: The UI uses React, lucide-react icons, @astryxdesign/core components, and virtua for the virtualized stream.

questions.question: What does baize depend on at runtime on the host besides Node?

expected.answer: System git (clone/fetch/worktrees), the CBM static binary (npm postinstall download), and optionally omp + Bun for chat.

questions.question: Which Node built-ins does the sync engine use for child processes?

expected.answer: node:child_process spawn with timeouts and kill handling in src/sync.js.

questions.question: Does the UI import any baize server code?

expected.answer: No — the SPA talks only over WebSocket/HTTP; ui/ is vendored Panda plus baize additions.

questions.question: What does the benchmark runner depend on?

expected.answer: ws for the ACP client, Node fetch for /api, and the dataset/report modules in src/benchmark/.

questions.question: If the shape of /api/repos changed, which code would be affected?

expected.answer: src/server.js handler, the /fleet page consumer in FLEET_HTML, the UI's baizeApi.ts, and the benchmark runner/report.

questions.question: What breaks if CBM's daemon switches cache-dir semantics?

expected.answer: Both src/cbm.js supervisor and the agent-injected server (src/agent-workspace.js env) must stay aligned on the same CBM_CACHE_DIR.

questions.question: Who is affected by changing the citation format in AGENTS.md?

expected.answer: src/agent-workspace.js prompt text, the UI unverified marker semantics, and the benchmark's extractCitations parser.

questions.question: What would renaming registry config fields (e.g. lastIndexedRevision) impact?

expected.answer: src/repos.js, config migration in src/config.js consumers, /api/repos response, fleet page, and prepareAgentWorkspace's table.

questions.question: If OMP stopped supporting session mcpServers, what is the fallback?

expected.answer: MCP injection (injectMcpServers) is the only wiring channel — the PRD §17 note records that project-level .omp/mcp.json is not loaded in ACP mode.

questions.question: Which tests guard the bridge injection behavior?

expected.answer: test/acp-bridge.test.js covers session/new|load|resume injection, client-wins, and pass-through of non-session methods.

questions.question: How does needs-auth handling work for fleet mirrors?

expected.answer: Git auth failures mark the repo needs-auth with exponential backoff; manual sync overrides the backoff; the PAT is never embedded in remote URLs.

questions.question: When does a repo re-index?

expected.answer: On every tracked-revision change via onRevision; same revision is a no-op; failures retry with exponential backoff aimed at the latest seen revision.

questions.question: How does the unverified marker decide a turn is unverified?

expected.answer: A settled turn (following turn exists or doc idle) that produced an agent_message, contains no tool_call and no turn_notice gets the marker.

questions.question: How is the PAT protected across the system?

expected.answer: config.json 0600; used only for GitLab API calls; never in git remote URLs, logs, or UI responses (gitlab.js sanitizes errors).

questions.question: What does the wizard's disk estimate show when GitLab withholds statistics?

expected.answer: sizeBytes is null — the summary says size unknown, or 'at least X (k/n report size)' for partial data; never zero.

questions.question: How does the first sync step avoid wedging on a failed start?

expected.answer: Start and poll errors are separate channels; a failed POST keeps its error with a Retry button; settled requires non-empty mirror states.

questions.question: Why do mirrors materialize linked worktrees?

expected.answer: CBM indexes readable checkouts; a bare mirror has no working tree, so sync adds a worktree at the tracked revision under ~/.baize/worktrees/.

questions.question: The chat answers without citations — where do you look first?

expected.answer: Check baize.log for the MCP injection line; a missing CBM binary logs the remedy; the UI marks such turns unverified.

questions.question: Indexing seems stuck after a GitLab outage — what state machines are involved?

expected.answer: The registry's retry backoff (retryAt) and the sync engine's needs-auth backoff both pause work; /api/repos shows retryAt and error.

questions.question: Two baize instances on one machine fight over the CBM daemon — why?

expected.answer: CBM's daemon is a per-account singleton bound to the first CBM_CACHE_DIR; a second cache dir cannot start until the first exits.

questions.question: A repo shows ready but searches return nothing — what could be wrong?

expected.answer: The agent may be querying a different project name (CBM normalizes slashes to dashes) or a stale index; check AGENTS.md and index stats.

questions.question: Wizard verify succeeds but discovery 404s — likely causes?

expected.answer: The group path may not exist or the PAT lacks read access to it; gitlab.js maps 404 to GITLAB_NOT_FOUND with the path echoed.

questions.question: The UI shows 'requires_action' but no permission card — what does that mean?

expected.answer: An elicitation is pending; the conversation is mid-flight, so the unverified marker stays hidden until the turn settles.

questions.question: Sync works from the fleet page but the agent sees no repos — why?

expected.answer: AGENTS.md is regenerated per connection; if the connection predates indexing, reconnect — or CBM binary resolution failed (check the log warn).

questions.question: How many HTTP endpoints does the management API expose?

expected.answer: Nine routes under /api: health, repos (GET/POST), gitlab settings/verify/discover, sync (GET/POST), sync/branch.

questions.question: Which files make up the benchmark harness?

expected.answer: src/benchmark/{dataset,run,report}.js plus run-cli.js/report-cli.js and benchmark/datasets/*.

questions.question: What test suites exist for the server?

expected.answer: test/*.test.js one per src module, plus test/fixtures/fake-agent.mjs and a CBM integration suite that skips without the binary.

questions.question: Which UI components did BaiZe add on top of Panda?

expected.answer: SetupWizard (+api/baizeApi), the unverified notice in MessageStream, and i18n keys for both.

questions.question: How is OMP telemetry disabled?

expected.answer: The overlay ~/.baize/omp-overlay.yml sets startup.checkUpdate false and the bridge scrubs OTEL_* env vars.

questions.question: What does the /fleet page offer that the wizard does not?

expected.answer: Ongoing management: sync now per repo/all, branch overrides, index state, adding local repos outside GitLab.

questions.question: Which logs does baize write and where?

expected.answer: ~/.baize/logs/baize.log — startup, requests, CBM/agent lifecycle, bridge injection lines.
